items.title: Drivers warn shouting for a taxi may become a catchcry of the past
paras: Tim Peachy says the business is struggling with the rising costs and heavy regulation faced by the taxi industry. ( ABC News: Rachel Holdsworth )
Taxi operators want a review into compulsory third party insurance and other regulations they say are unfair on point-to-point transport services.
A Wagga Wagga taxi operator says more towns are losing taxi services due to rising costs.
The NSW government is conducting a review into the Point-to-Point Transport Act.
Anyone who has dropped a beer in a country pub will have heard the familiar shout of "taxi".
But drivers and operators are warning the call may become a relic if changes are not made to protect the sector.
More than 20 taxi services across NSW have closed in the past few years, with many under significant strain.
Wagga Taxis CEO Tim Peachy, who operates in the NSW Riverina, said since rideshare companies arrived in Australia 10 years ago, operating a taxi business has become unfair.
Tim Peachy is concerned about the future of taxis in NSW. ( ABC NEWS: Rachel Holdsworth )
"Our running costs compared to their running costs, it's getting very hard to compete and very hard to keep our cars on the road," he said.
"Our green slips are over $5,000 in regional areas, in the cities even more.
"Rideshares are under private sector green slips and they're paying $500 to $700 a year."

A spokesperson for Uber, which represents 70 per cent of the rideshare market, said in a statement the company "recognises the cost pressures facing drivers and operators across the transport industry, and the important role point-to-point transport plays in keeping the community moving".
"We share the goal of keeping CTP insurance affordable, and sustainable."

Mr Peachey, along with other advocates, rallied at NSW Parliament earlier this week about inequity between the sector and rideshare companies, and the costs incurred to run a registered on-demand, point-to-point transport service.
Taxi operators and advocates converged at the State Parliament House in Macquarie Street to prompt change in the sector. ( Supplied: Tim Peachey )
He said the government needed to "level the playing field" because registered taxi services spent more to insure the cars, but setting up the service was more than just downloading an app.
Taxicabs are fitted with cameras as a legal requirement and the company must hold a license issued through the Point To Point Transport Commissioner.
"We go through a lot of checks at the start to become accredited as a taxi driver, most drivers work under a network and networks have very tight rules and regulations," Mr Peachey said.
"We do find a lot of female customers are coming back to us because they feel more safe and secure, especially with what's happened recently in rideshares without cameras.
In a statement, a NSW government spokesperson said it recognised the complexity of the issue and was conducting a statutory review of the Point to Point Act.
The spokesperson said the government's review would consider the issue in detail, including recommendations made in the NSW Legislative Council's review of the CTP scheme.
"Any reform to the CTP scheme must ensure it remains a vital safety net for people injured in a motor crash," the spokesperson said.
"Transport for NSW works closely with both rideshare operators and the taxi industry to improve services across NSW and ensure they continue to meet customer needs."
Mr Peachey said many towns in NSW had lost their taxi services in recent years, and more were being pushed to the brink.
"Just in the last two weeks, the Southern Highlands [Taxis] have closed their doors," he said.
Tim Peachey says many towns in NSW no longer have a taxi service. ( Datawrapper )
On Wednesday, Leeton Radio Cabs announced it would be forced to close due to rising costs.
"The fuel, and the CTP slip, they're all going up," co-owner Graeme Ahern said.
"They've all been going up for a while now, and it's just not worth it."
He said he still hoped to sell the business and did have an interested buyer.
Taxi drivers say the heavy regulations they face compared to rideshare companies is making it hard to compete. ( ABC News: Rachel Holdsworth )
In Temora, the taxi service closed down about two years ago, leaving locals to rely on only public transport.
Resident Sue Smith said the loss of the service was devastating, especially for older people who relied on the service.
"There's just been no interest in anyone setting up a cab [business] here at all, which is very difficult for older people," she said.

items.title: One Nation rules out deal with Coalition in NSW
paras: Mike Newman speaks at a firearms forum in Windsor on Saturday. ( ABC News )
One Nation's NSW leader Mike Newman has told a firearms forum the party "will never" form a coalition with the Coalition.
Mr Newman took a shot at Liberal leader Kellie Sloane, who lost an eighth MP last week.
The party has vowed to repeal post-Bondi Beach terror attack gun laws if elected.
One Nation New South Wales leader Mike Newman has ruled out a coalition with the Liberals and Nationals, as his party targets the vote of firearms owners.
Mr Newman made the comments at a community firearms forum hosted by One Nation at Windsor, in Sydney's west, on Saturday afternoon.
The former trade commissioner and investment banker was asked how he would hold the Coalition to account in a power-sharing arrangement.
He took a shot at the opposition over the exodus of Liberal MPs from state parliament.
"I've had texts backwards and forth with [opposition leader] Kellie Sloane, very kind of 'hi, how you going?' sort of thing, nothing serious," Mr Newman said.
"But it's clear eight of their sitting members are no longer contesting the next election. What does that send to their base as to how redundant they think their chances are?"
People attending One nation's firearms forum in Windsor on Saturday. ( ABC News: Alexander Lewis )
As the gun buyback scheme began this month, One Nation vowed to repeal the gun reforms brought in following the Bondi terror attack in December.
The party would abolish the general cap of four firearms per person and 10 for some licence holders, including sports shooters, pest controllers, and farmers.
It vowed to restore the maximum firearms licence term of five years, which had been lowered in July to two years.
One Nation would also reinstate appeals to the NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal (NCAT) for licence refusals or cancellations.
More than 500 guns were handed in during the gun buyback scheme's first week. ( Supplied: NSW Police )
Mr Newman is running for the Hunter seat of Cessnock, which has always been held by Labor — except for when Bob Roberts turned it Liberal in 1988.
The win was largely put down to the Unsworth Labor government's attempts to tighten gun laws in the wake of two mass shootings in Melbourne in 1987.
Labor ended up losing that election, and its tough stance on gun laws was seen by many as a "major contributing factor", according to a 1996 paper by the NSW Parliamentary Library Research Service.
Jeff Bacon, a Tamworth gun maker who is running for One Nation in the upper house, said gun laws would be an election issue, especially in regional areas.
"I have no doubt that it will impact and swap seats," Mr Bacon told the ABC.
Pistol shooter Geoff Neill, who lives in Georges Hall, said he used to vote Labor but no longer trusted the major party.
Former Labor voter Geoff Neill now supports One Nation. ( ABC News: Alexander Lewis )
"I think the people that are law abiding and have their guns should be allowed to keep them."
"I think they're more aligned with Labor than they need to be. I think if they were aligned with One Nation, One Nation being the core body that I trust right now," he said.
A day earlier, Opposition Leader Kellie Sloane distanced the Coalition from One Nation, reiterating her stance against a formal agreement.
"I've been consistent that we won't be forming a Coalition with One Nation," Ms Sloane said on Friday.
But like Mr Newman, she has left the door open to a supply and confidence agreement in the event that no-one wins a majority.
Mr Bacon said the post-Bondi laws had devastated his growing business, which he said had lost hundreds of thousands of dollars.
On Monday, the party promised to give "proper compensation" to firearms businesses, but it did not give a price tag.
While the government is offering grants of up to $25,000 for certain dealers, One Nation said the reforms had cost businesses about $320,000 on average, citing "industry research".
"Twenty-five grand is probably a month's revenue for some of these companies," Mr Newman said.
Mr Newman told the ABC the idea would be to compensate for losses, but he would not say how much a One Nation government would be prepared to pay.
"What those exact numbers will end up being, that'll be a matter at that time," he said.
"Of course it's an open-ended thing. But I don't think it's going to be anything that's outrageous," Mr Newman said.
"I believe the total amount of money that we would save from not embarking on a buyback … we think that compensation on the dealers alone would be a fraction of that number," he said.
Mr Newman revealed he met with the Parliamentary Budget Office this week, describing the independent costing body as "not fit for purpose" because it was working with limited information.
"If you've got a government organisation that is hamstrung with the information that is coming from it, it actually means they are not able to discharge their duties properly," Mr Newman said.
He said One Nation had yet to submit any policies to the PBO for costing but was "very happy to do so".

items.title: Troubled barramundi hatchery releases first fish in years
paras: Barramundi fingerlings have been successfully reared at Karumba for the first time in more than five years. ( Supplied: Les Wilson Barramundi Discovery Centre )
Barramundi fingerlings have been released into gulf waterways for the first time in five years.
Three thousand fingerlings were released after Karumba’s Les Wilson Barramundi Discovery Centre came back online.
Facility manager David Hammann expects to ramp up production capacity in the coming months.
Northern Queensland fishers will soon have access to more barramundi after a troubled Gulf hatchery released fingerlings for the first time in more than five years.

Karumba's Les Wilson Barramundi Discovery Centre is a major tourist attraction for the tiny Gulf town that allows visitors a chance to see how fish are caught, raised and released to replace stocks taken by anglers.
Carpentaria Shire Mayor Jack Bawden said in the past few years there was not a "single day" he did not regret taking over the asset in 2012, which was originally run by commercial fishers.
"We started off so well as a council-run show … then we hit on lean times with personnel more than anything," he said.
"There was always a reason, always an excuse [why fish didn't spawn] … and when you're ignorant like we are [about biology], you just have to accept it and continue on."
Late last year, council took a punt and promoted its own staff member and former commercial fisher David Hammann, who lacked formal aquaculture training, to get the facility running.
Since taking the reins last year, David Hammann has successfully released 3,000 fingerlings. ( ABC Rural: Abbey Halter )
After a year of trialling different tank sizes, new broodstock and employing what Mr Hammann described as "local secrets", the ex-fisherman released 3,000 fingerlings into local wetlands last week.
"It's been a long time between drinks, let me tell you," Cr Bawden said.
"It doesn't sound like a lot but, by God, it's an improvement for what we've had."
Jack Bawden (left) says the hatchery was originally established as a way to replenish local stocks removed by anglers. ( Supplied: Carpentaria Shire Council )
After the early success, Mr Hammann said he was planning to ramp up production.
"We have a permit for the Norman River, [where] we can release up to 100,000 … and over at Burketown we can do another 100,000 there," he said.
"Hopefully next season we'll be looking into getting those quotas filled."
To successfully rear barramundi, wild broodstock are collected from around the Southern Gulf. ( ABC North West Queensland: Emily Dobson )
The centre works exclusively with Southern Gulf of Carpentaria barramundi, a distinct stock from east coast fish that require warmer conditions.
Mr Hammann said wild barramundi were first netted to find the best possible parents, before stronger females were picked.
"We separate the females and males out and cannulate them for egg quality," he said.
"If they've got good egg quality … 400 microns and a bit bigger … we go ahead and start hormone injections and wait until they start spawning."
David Hammann says the surplus of reeds and structure means the fingerlings have a good chance of survival against predators. ( Supplied: Carpentaria shire council )
The hatcheries renaissance is not just a win for Gulf waterways; it's a lifeline to the lakes and dams across the North West.
Prior to 2020, the barramundi centre provided low-cost fingerlings to fishing groups in Mount Isa and Cloncurry to stock local water bodies.
Mount Isa's Lake Moondarra has not been restocked with barramundi for years, creating a pool of large, lure-wise fish.
Years without re-stocking means a number of large fish still exist in the lake, but few medium and small fish remain. ( Supplied: Scott Grech )
Mount Isa Fish Stocking Committee president Mick Scotney said if more fingerlings could be produced and shipped south in coming months, it would completely change anglers' experiences.
"Chasing big barramundi is one type of fishing, but you can definitely increase the experience with the different sizes as they grow," he said.
"It also makes it a lot more sustainable because the big fish are more susceptible to the fish kills … the really cold winters and low lake levels."
Mr Scotney said the news was "exciting" but after years of false starts he still had contingencies.
"It is very exciting that Karumba has managed to breed fish after five or six years, but we are working on a plan B," he said.
"We'll have barramundi fingerlings in the dam one way or another … in the next 12 months."

items.title: Bystanders pull male driver from burning car in Canberra
paras: Police say the car caught fire after crashing into trees, and bystanders rushed to pull the driver from the blaze. ( ABC News: Mark Moore )
Police are commending the actions of bystanders who rushed in to pull a male driver from a burning car in Canberra's inner north this morning.
ACT Policing says a grey Mazda 3 left the road and crashed into trees on Antill Street between the intersections of Phillip Avenue and Cadell Street in Downer about 6:10am.
The vehicle caught alight and police say bystanders rushed in to pull the unconscious driver to safety.
"I really want to commend the actions of the members of the public who were first on scene, who pulled [the man] from the vehicle," Acting Inspector Joel Wiseman said.
ACT Policing's major collisions team is investigating the cause of the crash. ( ABC News: Mark Moore )
A section of Antill Street remains closed in both directions as ACT Policing's major collisions team investigates.
Anyone who witnessed a grey Mazda 3 travelling in the Dickson area about 6am is urged to contact Crime Stoppers.
Police say the grey Mazda 3 left the road and crashed into trees on Antill Street about 6:10am. ( ABC News: Mark Moore )
The crash comes just three days after a cyclist was killed in a collision with a car on the Federal Highway near Horse Park Drive .
"I just want to remind Canberra drivers to please ensure that they're driving to the conditions of the roads," Acting Inspector Wiseman said.

"Unfortunately we've had 13 fatalities in the ACT for this year, and we're pleading with the Canberra community to make sure they're driving safely — we want you all to return home to your family and loved ones."

items.title: Sarah advertised for a roommate. The love of her life applied
paras: Billy, 31, and Sarah, 32, are based in regional Queensland. ( Supplied )
Sarah didn't list "love of my life" as one of the criteria when advertising for a roommate. But applicant Billy ended up being just that.
Whether it's romantic, platonic, heartbreaking or surprising, our Love Story series is about love in all its forms. Share yours with us .
Sarah: I was moving out of my parents' house into a home I'd built and was looking for someone to share the costs with. I also didn't want to live alone.
Originally, I thought I would find a girl around my age, working full time, and that would be fun.
When Billy applied, I saw he had a good job. He looked really friendly and in his application he said, "I know you asked for women, but just wondering if you would consider me."
Billy: Sarah's ad was well written and painted a great picture of the place. She sounded like a nice person.
When I arrived to take a look, she had a bubbly personality and it was a beautiful place. It felt like somewhere that could be home straight away.
Sarah didn’t want to live with a man at first, but says Billy felt safe. ( Supplied )
Sarah: Billy was so polite, complimenting the house — that was making me feel good.
He was offering things like, "What do you want to do with the plates? Do you want me to use yours, bring my own, or I could buy ones that match what you have?"
Sarah: From the very first night we really hit it off. In a matter of two weeks, we went from strangers to practically family.
I thought I liked him, but I wasn't necessarily thinking it would go to the next level.
The logical part of my brain was like, don't even go there because you're housemates.
Billy: I had a similar view. We're housemates, I need somewhere to live, if this doesn't quite work out … is that a risk worth taking?
One night Sarah had gone to have a shower and came and said goodnight and went to bed.
I knocked on her door and said, "Do you reckon you'd have more time for more of a chat?"
Her reaction was a bit like, "Really? We just chatted for five hours, is there more you want to discuss?"
Sarah: He said, "Oh, I just feel like we're getting along very well. I'm single and you're single. I wondered if you'd be interested in taking things to the next level?"
I had thought we might have a few drinks one night and see what happens. I wasn't expecting a sober weeknight confrontation.
But he is very gentlemanly. He always tries to do things in a respectful manner.
I said I would think about it. He said to take my time. Over the coming weeks it just progressed.
Sarah: What I love most about Billy is that if you meet him, you will think he's very quiet and reserved. But behind closed doors he's very silly, playful and childlike.
He brings a lot of energy into the house. He's a morning person, so I'll wake up and he's singing — very bright and bubbly.
We're both very family orientated and love being in our house together.
We work from home, all day every day, and never really get sick of each other.
She lives very much in the moment. If she gets a phone call from a friend, she'll run down the hallway, kick off her shoes and jump on her bed.
There are little tokens around to show she's been there. It gives our house that homely feeling.
Sarah: We got engaged in February so are planning a wedding. And we do plan to have children as well.
While we are looking forward to the future, I feel like everything now is perfect. My Nan is still alive at 90, our parents are healthy — we are trying to really absorb the things we have.
Billy: I'm looking forward to simply growing old with my person. And having my best friend and person beside me through life.
We often talk about the worries of family members getting older, but at least we will have each other.
Life is going to throw curveballs at us, and we will have each other to work through things.

items.title: Reserve Bank issues Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) (Second Amendment) Regulations
paras: The Foreign Exchange Management (Export of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2015 were superseded by the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026, which were issued on January 13, 2026 , and became effective from October 01, 2026. The new regulations are principle based; intended to promote ease of doing business, especially for small exporters and importers; and empower Authorised Dealers to provide quicker and more efficient service to their customers. Based on subsequent feedback received from stakeholders, the Reserve Bank has issued Amendment Regulations to Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026 that were notified on November 02, 2026 , and came into effect, retrospectively, from October 01, 2026 . In this regard, to facilitate better understanding of the new trade regulations by the exporters/importers and other stakeholders, the Reserve Bank has placed a Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026 on its website. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1531

items.title: RBI imposes monetary penalty on Fusion Finance Limited
paras: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has, by an order dated November 17, 2026, imposed a monetary penalty of ₹7.50 lakh (Rupees Seven Lakh Fifty Thousand only) on Fusion Finance Limited (the company) for non-compliance with certain provisions of directions issued by RBI on ‘Know Your Customer (KYC)’ and ‘Internal Ombudsman’. This penalty has been imposed in exercise of powers conferred on RBI under section 58G(1)(b) read with section 58B(5)(aa) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. The statutory inspection of the company was conducted by RBI with reference to its financial position as on March 31, 2026. Based on the supervisory findings of non-compliance with RBI directions and related correspondence in that regard, a notice was issued to the company advising it to show cause as to why penalty should not be imposed on it for failure to comply with the RBI directions. After considering the company's reply to the notice, additional submissions made by it and oral submissions made during the personal hearing, RBI found that the following charges against the company were sustained, warranting imposition of monetary penalty: The company failed to obtain PAN or equivalent e-document thereof or Form 60 from customers, while establishing an account-based relationship with those customers; and, The company failed to escalate the partly or wholly rejected complaints to the Internal Ombudsman for a final decision within the prescribed time. This action is based on deficiencies in regulatory compliance and is not intended to pronounce upon the validity of any transaction or agreement entered into by the company with its customers. Further, imposition of this monetary penalty is without prejudice to any other action that may be initiated by RBI against the company. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1537

items.title: Indian students in Kazan delighted as PM Modi arrives for BRICS Summit
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Kazan [ Russia ], October 22 (ANI): Indian students in Kazan , Russia , are happy and excited about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival at Hotel Korston , as he attends the 16th BRICS Summit . Notably, PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday touched down in Kazan city of Russia to participate in the 16th BRICS Summit and received a warm welcome. He is here to attend the 16th BRICS Summit , being held under the Chairmanship of Russia . To welcome PM Modi , students from India studying in Russia also sang a welcome song as they awaited PM Modi 's arrival at Hotel Korston . An Indian student from Pune, Saniya said that the students are quite excited to greet PM Modi . "Maybe we will get the opportunity (to meet PM Modi ) as many students are here (at Hotel Korston )... We are very excited. We are lucky to have this opportunity and we are happy to see him," she told ANI. An Indian student from Bihar, Shaurya Pratap said, "We are very happy to welcome PM Modi and we have prepared a song for him and we hope he likes it." Surbhi from Delhi said, "I have been here in Kazan since 2019 and today, we are going to sing a song for PM Modi and we are very excited about that." Parul, a final-year medical student, who has been in Kazan for the last five years told ANI, "We are really grateful that we got this opportunity to welcome our dear Prime Minister." Arti Pawar from Maharashtra said, "I have been living here for the past three years. I am very happy that PM Modi is coming here." Mrunmayi from Nagpur, Maharashtra said, "All the students here are quite enthusiastic as PM is going to come soon. We are too much delighted to welcome him." Meanwhile, ISKCON volunteers - from the Russia n and Indian communities were seen chanting 'Hare Krishna, Hare Ram' ahead of PM Modi 's arrival. While speaking with ANI, Sergoy, an ISKCON volunteer, said, "'Hare Krishna is a Mahamantra. This visit of PM Modi to Kazan , Russia is an important one for us. We are happy." Another ISKCON volunteer said, "We want to welcome PM Modi here in Kazan . It's a great honour for us to welcome him here We are very excited to see him." A Russia n citizen, Alexander said that the people there will welcome PM Modi by singing a song and that he is happy with PM Modi 's visit to Kazan . He said, "We have made a banner and we will also sing a song to welcome PM Modi ... I returned from India just two days back and directly came from Delhi to Kazan to see PM Modi . I am very happy that he is coming to Russia ." Notably, ahead of his departure to Russia , PM Modi shared a post on X and wrote, "Leaving for Kazan , Russia , to take part in the BRICS Summit . India attaches immense importance to BRICS, and I look forward to extensive discussions on a wide range of subjects. I also look forward to meeting various leaders there." The Prime Minister's office in a statement quoted PM Modi as saying, "I am departing today on a two-day visit to Kazan at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russia n Federation, to attend the 16th BRICS Summit ." "India values the close cooperation within BRICS which has emerged as an important platform for dialogue and discussion on issues concerning the global developmental agenda, reformed multilateralism, climate change, economic cooperation, building resilient supply chains, promoting cultural and people to people connect, among others," PM Modi said. The statement further said that the expansion of BRICS with the addition of new members last year has added to its inclusivity and agenda for the global good. "Building upon the Annual Summit held in July 2024 in Moscow, my visit to Kazan will further reinforce the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia . I look forward to meeting other leaders from BRICS as well," the PMO statement said. The 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan is being held under the chairmanship of Russia from October 22-24. During his visit, PM Modi is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from BRICS member countries and invited leaders in Kazan . The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "The Summit, themed 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security,' will provide an important platform for leaders to discuss key global issues." It further said, "The Summit will offer a valuable opportunity to assess the progress of initiatives launched by BRICS and to identify potential areas for future collaboration." This visit marks, PM Modi 's second visit to Russia this year. He travelled to Moscow in July to attend the 22nd India- Russia Annual Summit where he held a bilateral meeting with President Putin. He was also conferred with Russia 's highest civilian award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle at the Kremlin in Moscow. BRIC, as a formal grouping, started after the meeting of the Leaders of Russia , India and China in St Petersburg on the margins of G8 Outreach Summit in 2006. The grouping was formalized during the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the margins of UNGA in New York in 2006. The first BRIC Summit was held in Russia 's Yekaterinburg in 2009. It was agreed to expand BRIC into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa at the BRIC Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York in 2010. South Africa attended the 3rd BRICS Summit in Sanya in 2011. A further expansion of BRICS took place in 2024 with five new members - Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. (ANI)

items.title: "Singapore plays key role in Act-East policy": Rajnath Singh at India-Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Dr. Ng Eng Hen , Singapore 's Minister of Defence , has begun his three-day visit to India . As part of his visit, Dr. Hen co-chaired the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, with his India n counterpart Rajnath Singh . The Summit began on Tuesday morning, with India n Defence Minister Rajnath Singh welcoming the Singapore delegation warmly. He noted that the strategic partnership the two countries share is a "testimony of increasing closeness between our countries." Singh said, " The meeting is happening at a time when India marks the decade of India 's Act in Policy, in which Singapore has played a key role in promoting economic cooperation, cultural ties, and developed strategic connectivity with country institutions." Building upon Singh's remarks, Dr. Ng Eng Hen said, "You reminded us that this is the 10th year since your Act East Policy. From Singapore 's perspective, India has always been part of the East. Whether you choose to act or look, we consider you part of the area." He said that while remembering the history of Singapore , India has been an important partner. " When we started the Singapore armed forces, one of the countries that we asked early on to see whether they could help us was India ." Hen highlighted that such historical memoirs serve as important reminders and "reflects how we feel that India is very part of our area. We are delighted that our ten years of bilateral relations have been very much improved in defence and all-round strategic partnership." Hen also thanked PM Modi for visiting Singapore earlier this year and noted that the visit was an excellent meeting. A day before, the Ministry of Defence had announced the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi on October 22, 2024. The release noted that between India and Singapore , "The engagements have diversified to include wide-ranging contacts between the Services, military-to-military exchanges, high-level visits, capacity building and training programs, cooperation in UN Peacekeeping, ship visits and bilateral exercises." Inaugurated in 2016, the India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue is a key platform to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between Singapore and India . The fifth edition of the Defence Ministers' Dialogue took place in January 2021 through virtual teleconference. During the meeting, the two parties showed confidence in the outcomes of the meeting that would result in providing impetus to the entire spectrum of the bilateral engagement as well as to the regional security architecture. (ANI)

items.title: India sends humanitarian aid to Palestine; consignment comprises 30 tons of essential items
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, India took a significant step in providing humanitarian aid for the people of Palestine. This initial consignment comprises 30 tons of essential items, including medicines, surgical supplies, dental products, general medical items, and high-energy biscuits, which will be distributed through the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA). Sharing a post on X, Randhir Jaiswal, the official spokesperson of the Ministry of External Affairs wrote, "India sends humanitarian assistance for the people of Palestine through UNRWA." "The first tranche of assistance comprising 30 tons of medicine and food items has departed today. The consignment includes a wide range of essential medicines and surgical supplies, dental products, general medical items and high-energy biscuits," the post added.

🇮🇳 sends humanitarian assistance for the people of Palestine through UNRWA. The first tranche of assistance comprising 30 tons of medicine and food items has departed today. The consignment includes a wide range of essential medicines and surgical supplies, dental products,… pic.twitter.com/ZlFiKOfezx

Notably, a few days ago, the World Food Programme issued a warning for northern Gaza, saying that WFP's supplies are depleting. Sharing a post on X on October 12, WFP wrote, "Escalating violence in northern #Gaza is having a disastrous impact on food security. No food aid has entered the north since 1 October. It is unclear how long WFP's remaining food supplies in the north, already distributed to shelters and health facilities, will last." Earlier on October 20, the United Nations renewed its call for an end to the war in Gaza, emphasising the urgent need for the release of hostages, the cessation of the displacement of Palestinians, and the unhindered delivery of humanitarian aid. In a statement released by the UN Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process, Tor Wennesland, the UN expressed deep concern, stating, "The nightmare in Gaza is intensifying. Horrifying scenes are unfolding in the northern Strip amidst conflict, relentless Israeli strikes and an ever-worsening humanitarian crisis." Last month, UNRWA had said people in Gaza are living in "inhumane" conditions. The agency said on the social media platform X that piles of waste are accumulating in central Gaza, while sewage water is leaking into the streets. "Families have no choice but to live next to this accumulated waste, exposing them to foul odours and the imminent risk of a health disaster," the UNWRA added. The UN agency called for an immediate ceasefire. (ANI)

items.title: India is the top market for investment globally: Mark Mobius
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Mark Mobius, Founder of Mobius Capital Partners LLP , and an ace investor with expertise in emerging markets said, India's is the top stock market globally where he would like to invest. In an exclusive interview with ANI, the octagenarian said, "India would have to come first when I think about investment," Mobius stated, "Of course, India would have to be the first choice. Then, I would probably look at Taiwan. It's a Chinese society, but it's a free society and they're doing very well. Now we're beginning to see China rise again. There will be some interesting companies in China, but still, India remains our top pick." Mobius highlighted technology as his favorite sector to invest in India. "In the future, I believe there's going to be significant growth in hardware technology. As you know, India is already strong in software technology, but moving forward, hardware manufacturing will gain momentum here in India," he said. Discussing India's semiconductor infrastructure, Mobius mentioned that it is already developing. "Many of the world's large semiconductor companies already have software development operations in India, employing thousands of software engineers. The next step, of course, is hardware. Soon, we'll see large semiconductor manufacturing plants. The scale of investment we're talking about isn't in the millions, but billions of dollars, to produce the most advanced semiconductors in the world." Mobius also fondly remembered Ratan Tata, who passed away this month. "I met him many years ago and found him to be a very friendly, humble, and insightful person. I was deeply saddened to hear about his passing. I considered him one of the great Indian entrepreneurs of the century," Mobius added. Earlier on Monday, Mark Mobius, speaking at the NDTV World Summit 2024, reiterated he was bullish on India's real estate and semiconductor sectors, as he outlined the potential of these two key industries. In the semiconductor space, he said fabrication companies (fabs) will come here because India has got the population and the labour force. The octagenarian believes India will become "the leader" of the semiconductor industry. The government has so far approved five semiconductor units in India, of which construction in two sites is on, and soon the work in the other three will start. The companies have already made a cumulative investment of almost Rs 1.5 lakh crore. While talking about the parameters he looks at while investing in companies, Mobius said he looks at the growth of earnings in companies, along with the return on capital invested, and the quality of management. Asked about his investment advice to his "younger self," Mobius said, "Don't be in a rush, and study carefully". He added that one has to listen to the market. (ANI)

items.title: Mukka Proteins Limited Announces Rs 98 Crore Preferential Issue for Acquisition and Expansion
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel VMPL Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 22: Mukka Proteins Limited , India's largest fish meal and insect meal producer and a leader in the animal protein industry , has announced the approval of a preferential issue worth Rs 98 crore by its Board of Directors. This strategic move will help Mukka Proteins in its ongoing domestic and international acquisition and expansion efforts, reinforcing its position in the global market. A significant portion of the funding will come from the promoter and promoter group, underlining their commitment to the company's robust growth strategy. The preferential issue will comprise up to 1.96 crore equity shares at Rs50 per share, aggregating to Rs98 crore. This price includes a premium of Rs49 per share on the face value of Rs1. Mukka Proteins will use the raised capital to enhance production capabilities and meet the growing global demand for sustainable and high-quality protein solutions, particularly in the fishmeal and insect meal sectors. In a clear show of confidence, Mukka Proteins' promoters have committed to a capital infusion of INR 60 crore through a preferential allotment of equity shares. This significant financial backing will be used to strengthen the company's financial position, reduce debt, and fund key operational improvements. Mukka Proteins has consistently embraced sustainability, having commercialized insect protein as a significant innovation for the aquaculture and animal feed industry. The company's waste-to-food initiatives have contributed to environmental sustainability, particularly in collaboration with the Mangaluru municipality for waste management. These efforts not only align with global environmental best practices but also enhance circular economy processes, focusing on converting municipal waste into valuable protein and oil products. Mukka Proteins is known for its strong commitment to ecological preservation, evident through the development of sustainable products such as fishmeal, fish oil, and insect protein. As a key player in the aquaculture and nutraceutical markets, Mukka contributes 25-30% of the market share in India's fishmeal and fish oil industry. The company plans to expand its operations further, capitalizing on this capital infusion to enter new markets and enhance its global footprint.

This issuance is subject to necessary statutory and regulatory approvals, including shareholder approval at the upcoming Extra-Ordinary General Meeting (EGM) on November 16, 2024. Managing Director and CEO Harris commented, "This preferential issue is a major milestone for Mukka Proteins as we continue to strengthen our market position. Our growth plans remain firmly rooted in sustainability, and this capital will enable us to scale up production, diversify our product offerings, and reinforce our commitment to responsible and eco-friendly business practices." Mukka Proteins Limited is poised to capture new opportunities in the animal protein sector, reinforcing its legacy of innovation, sustainability, and operational excellence. Mukka Proteins Limited : Mukka Proteins Limited is a leading manufacturer and exporter of fish meal , fish oil, and other protein products. The company has built a reputation for delivering high-quality, sustainable protein products to a global customer base. With a commitment to innovation and quality, Mukka Proteins serves industries including aquaculture, pet food, and agriculture across multiple continents. Headquartered in Mangalore, India, Mukka Proteins operates state-of-the-art processing facilities that meet stringent international standards. The company is dedicated to sustainable practices and has been at the forefront of environmental stewardship within the protein processing industry. items.title: Review: Godzilla Minus Zero joins the list of truly stellar sequels
paras: long may he roar Review: Godzilla Minus Zero joins the list of truly stellar sequels Director Takashi Yamazaki ups the ante by pitting Godzilla against one of the monster’s greatest foes

17 ... ... ... Credit: Toho Credit: Toho Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav It’s a rare thing for a film sequel to match or even surpass its predecessor; The Godfather Part II and Terminator 2: Judgement Day are the best known examples on a pretty short list. Go ahead and add Godzilla Minus Zero to that list. Director Takashi Yamazaki’s sequel to his critically acclaimed Godzilla Minus One (2023) is everything one could want in a Godzilla movie: human pathos, great special effects, and, ultimately, two giant kaiju duking it out over who gets to destroy Japan (and eventually the world) the most.
(Spoilers for the first film below. Spoilers for Minus Zero but no major reveals until after the gallery. We’ll give you a heads-up when we get there.)

As I wrote previously , Yamazaki wanted to return to Godzilla’s filmic roots with Minus One , setting the events in postwar Japan and tapping into the monster’s symbolic representation of the Japanese perspective on the 1940s nuclear holocaust—while also incorporating all-too-human themes of guilt and redemption. That first film focused on kamikaze pilot Kōichi Shikishima (Ryunosuke Kamiki), who struggled with survivor’s guilt after he failed to take action when Godzilla attacked the Japanese base on Odo Island in 1945.

Knocked unconscious, Kōichi survived and awoke to find his parents and many others were killed in the World War II bombing of Tokyo. Kōichi rebuilt a life with a woman named Noriko (Minami Hamabe) and the orphaned baby she rescued, Akiko (Sae Nagatani). But then Godzilla re-emerged, and Kōichi resolved to die fighting the monster to atone for Odo Island. Kōichi saved the day and lived to tell the tale. He reunited with Noriko, who had a strange black bruise on her neck. And we saw a chunk of Godzilla’s remains start to regenerate, leaving things open for a sequel.

Godzilla Minus On e was a massive hit, both in Japan—where it remains one of the highest grossing Japanese films ever—and worldwide, racking up $116 million globally and winning an Oscar for best visual effects. Yamazaki said in interviews at the time that there had as yet been no talk of a sequel—while also hinting at future directions a sequel might explore. He later admitted it was way of planting a seed for what would become Godzilla Minus Zero .

Godzilla Minus Zero is set two years after the events of the first film, with Kamiki and Hamabe reprising their roles as Kōichi and Noriko, along with Nagatani as Akiko. The family is just trying to live in peace after the devastation Godzilla inflicted on their country. Alas, a new kaiju emerges, arriving via meteorite and using its tentacles to feed on local wildlife before morphing into a dragon-like creature that causes fresh rampaging destruction. Fans of the genre will recognize this creature as Ghidorah , whose appearance in the film was teased in the various trailers.

It isn’t long before Kenji Noda (Hidetaka Yoshioka)—i.e., the dude with the magnificent wavy gray hair who is director of the Large-Scale Disaster Response Bureau—seeks out Kōichi for help in dealing with this new kaiju threat. His team is able to track Ghidorah’s movements via electrical storms and other pertinent weather patterns, thanks to meteorologist Makoto Aoyama (Masami Nagasawa). But the team has no idea how they might defeat this new threat to life and infrastructure. It’s hardly a spoiler to note that at some point, a regenerated Godzilla will come into play.
(WARNING: significant spoilers appear below. Stop reading now if you haven’t seen the film.)

Ryunosuke Kamiki reprises his role as former kamikaze pilot Kōichi Shikishima Minami Hamabe as his wife, Noriko Minami Hamabe as his wife, Noriko Sae Nagatani as Akiko Sae Nagatani as Akiko Minami Hamabe as his wife, Noriko Sae Nagatani as Akiko Still the best hair in the entire cast: Hidetaka Yoshioka as Kenji Noda, director of the Large-Scale Disaster Response Bureau Min Tanaka as biologist Kanji Murakami Masami Nagasawa as Makoto Aoyama King Ghidorah mutates into his three-headed form Levitating buildings seems to be Ghidorah’s superpower Godzilla rises from the ocean depths to battle Ghidorah. Yamazaki has retained the visual tone that made the film’s predecessor so striking; it feels like classic Godzilla fare of yore, just with 21st century cutting-edge visual effects. If anything, he’s upped his game on the special effects front, reflecting the larger production budget he had to work with. (It’s also the first Japanese movie filmed specifically for IMAX and it’s well-worth seeing in that format.)

Much of that budget went toward bringing the central monsters to cinematic life, and Godzilla Minus Zero does not disappoint. Ghidorah, for instance, responds to a bombing attack by mutating into its famous three-headed King Ghidorah form, complete with a spiffy new superpower: a “gravity beam” that lets the creature levitate entire houses (and, at one point, Godzilla) into the sky before dropping them back to the ground. And the kaiju vs. kaiju battle is spectacular in both scope and execution.

Yamazaki even managed to squeeze in what he called his “bucket-list” special effects shot inspired by a scene in 2008’s Cloverfield : Godzilla looming out of the Atlantic Ocean in front of the Statue of Liberty to wreck havoc on the statue and New York City in general. Granted, it occurs in a dream sequence of biologist Kanji Murakami (Min Tanaka), who survived the Hiroshima blast that killed his wife and children and longs for revenge. And it’s not just indulgence on the director’s part: the scene reinforces the traditional theme of linking Godzilla to nuclear radiation and the horrors of the atomic bomb.

Nor does Yamazaki ignore the human factor via the dilemma of his nuclear family trio. Kōichi must wrestle with his conscience: how can he risk his life again to battle a kaiju when it could mean leaving Akiko an orphan yet again should he fail? Noriko is infected with Godzilla’s radioactive G-cells—the only human to survive the mutations in her own body for so long. But her time could be running out, plus they’ve kept her infection secret for fear she will be taken away by the government for experimentation. Sometimes doing the right thing comes at great personal cost, and watching these quite ordinary people grapple with that reality brings emotional depth to the film.

The film ends on a suitably bittersweet note, and while Yamazaki hasn’t dropped any hints about a possible third film in the series, we’d love to learn more about Noriko’s strangely symbiotic connection to Godzilla via the G-cells in her bloodstream. Long may he reign.

items.title: Alexander Zverev calls out the misconception people have about him ahead of facing Carlos Alcaraz
paras: Alexander Zverev will face Carlos Alcaraz in a blockbuster final at the ATP Finals this year.
Zverev beat Daniil Medvedev 7-6(0), 6-4 to reach the final of the ATP Finals for the third time in his career and for the first time since he won his second title at the year-end tournament in 2021.

It will be in this final where Zverev will face Alcaraz , who is currently on a 13-match winning streak after his latest win over Ben Shelton . Zverev is yet to beat Alcaraz or Jannik Sinner this year, and he has called out a misconception he thinks people have about him after setting up a meeting against the former in the final of the ATP Finals. Do you believe that Alexander Zverev will win Grand Slams in 2027 with Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz back?
items.impact: The last time Zverev faced Alcaraz was in the Australian Open semi-finals this year, where he was beaten by the Spaniard in a five-hour and 27-minute classic after serving for the match.

items.title: Daniil Medvedev doesn’t believe Alexander Zverev has improved in one area, ‘I wouldn’t say it’s better’
paras: Daniil Medvedev lost to Alexander Zverev in the ATP Finals semi-finals. The Russian star is a former ATP Finals champion, but he won’t add to his 2020 triumph this weekend. Zverev defeated Medvedev , 7-6 (7-0), 6-4, in Turin, taking control when it mattered most.

After the match, Medvedev was asked several questions about Zverev’s game during his press conference. One journalist asked the world number five whether he believed Zverev’s forehand had improved. I think I will put it this way: I think his forehand was very good even before, and then sometimes he can miss.

Today he also missed a couple, so I would not say it’s better,” said Medvedev. Medvedev has a point, as evidenced by the statistics from his semi-final defeat to Zverev . The German hit six forehand winners, but seven forehand unforced errors on Friday evening.

items.title: “Deserved to lose”: Medvedev bows to a Zverev who won’t be broken
paras: Daniil Medvedev did not look for excuses after his 7-6(0), 6-4 defeat by Alexander Zverev in the ATP Finals semi-finals in Turin. The German, unbroken all week and already focused on Carlos Alcaraz, looked back on the Melbourne loss that set his season in motion.

Medvedev “[I] deserved to lose.” Daniil Medvedev did not look for excuses after his 7-6(0), 6-4 defeat in the ATP Finals semi-finals on Saturday. The Russian never got a look at a break point against Alexander Zverev , who has not lost his serve all week in Turin, and he pointed to the two moments where the match got away from him.
“I said even before the match, serve is important,” he said in his press conference. “Sasha didn’t get broken yet this tournament, so not easy.

items.title: Alexander Zverev joins Jannik Sinner and Novak Djokovic on legendary list as he reaches ATP Finals final
paras: Alexander Zverev defeated Daniil Medvedev, 7-6, 6-4, in the ATP Finals semi-finals. The world number one edged a tight match in Turin to advance to his third ATP Finals final and his first since 2021.

Zverev was better in the key moments of his semi-final match, particularly in the first-set tiebreak, which he won 7-0. Zverev didn’t face a break point against Medvedev, and has yet to be broken in Turin.

Reaching the final of the ATP Finals without being broken, the German wrote his name into the history books. Since 2000, only three men have qualified for the ATP Finals final without being broken: Zverev, Jannik Sinner , and Novak Djokovic. Sinner held serve until the final last year, and Djokovic did the same back in 2018. But who did Sinner and Djokovic beat on their way to the final, and did their serve hold up with the title on the line?

Friendships are built by repeated contact, not by being liked
items.hook: This is the single most useful fact in the whole guide.
paras: Studies of primary-school classrooms found that children seated next to each other were far more likely to become friends than children seated across the room. When teachers changed the seating, new friendships formed with the new neighbours.

So the engine is: same place, same people, same activity, over and over. The day at the yo-yo bar followed by basketball is that engine working - shared activity changed how the other boy treated him. It was not luck.
items.do: Pick one activity he already likes and commit to it weekly for a full term.

items.title: Keep the proximity - change the watching
items.hook: Your instinct is half right, and the other half matters.
paras: You are right that being around the group matters: children nominate as friends the children they see and interact with most. 'Out of sight, out of mind' is real for acquaintances.

But guidance written for schools is blunt: merely remaining beside a group is not friendship. A child who hovers is read as a bystander rather than a player, and it holds him in the one-down position. Watching has a use - but only as the first twenty seconds of joining in, never as the endpoint.
items.do: Keep telling him to stay near the group. Add: 'then take a job in the game'.

items.title: Teach 'watch, then blend'
items.hook: The best way to join a game is not to ask.
paras: Most of us were told to walk up and say 'Can I play?' But that makes everyone stop and look at him, and makes 'no' very easy.

The better sequence, used by people who study play: watch for about twenty seconds to learn the game and where the line is, then slide into the action without stopping it. Take the end of the line. Stand in the outfield. Pick up the ball and pass it back.
items.do: Rehearse it at home in five minutes. Ask him to name the 'easiest job' in each game.

items.title: Host one friend at a time - this is the biggest lever you control
items.hook: The child who invites is rarely short of friends.
paras: Pick a child he has had fun with in the last month, not someone he admires from afar. Invite one person for one to two hours. Put away anything precious, have two activities ready, start with a snack, and let the guest choose sometimes.
Keep it short and end while they are both still enjoying it. Then leave a few weeks before inviting the same child again, so the invitation can come back to him.
items.do: Text one parent this week and set a date for the school holidays.

items.title: Ask the teacher one specific question
items.hook: Teachers see the playground. Ask them to name names.
paras: Ask two things: who does he play well with, and could he be seated near them or paired with them for group work?
Seating is one of the few levers that reliably creates new friendships, and it is invisible to the children - no one has to know it was arranged.
items.do: Email the teacher this week with those two questions.

items.title: Do not push into a group that is rejecting him
items.hook: Here the advice is the opposite of persistence.
paras: Where a group is actively excluding him, the guidance is to back off - when you back off from people, they can move towards you. Put his energy into two or three other children instead of one closed circle.
Friends in more than one place - school, a club, family friends - also make him far less vulnerable when one group turns cold.
items.do: Help him list three children outside the difficult group he could get to know.

items.title: One or two good friends is the goal - not popularity
paras: Kids need one or two good friends. You do not need to worry about him being the most popular child in the class.
His warmth and kindness are already the raw material. Treat this as coaching a skill, not fixing a fault - if he feels like a project, he will resist.
items.do: Say his strengths out loud, often. Confidence is what carries a child into a group.

items.title: Playing and talking with girls is normal and good
items.hook: Children believe gender matters far more than it actually does.
paras: In one large classroom experiment, simply seating boys and girls next to each other doubled how often they became friends.
Girls' play tends to build conversation, turn-taking and inventing games together; boys' play builds bigger, faster group play. Being good at both widens his circle.
items.do: No action needed. Just do not let him think it is odd.

items.title: When to get more help
items.hook: Ordinary friendship difficulty is not a disorder.
paras: Get more support if he becomes reluctant to go to school, is persistently distressed, has changes in sleep or appetite, or says it is happening all the time and he cannot make it stop.
Start with his teacher, then the school counsellor, then your GP for a referral. Kids Helpline is free and open 24/7 on 1800 55 1800, for children and for parents.
items.do: Save Kids Helpline in your phone: 1800 55 1800.
